decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation: “Save a bookmark (P1) — paste a URL”; round 1 response retains the save workflow while requesting additions.
decisions.note: Conforming URL-save decision at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation only says “missing titles auto-derived.” Round 1 response requires automatic “title, description, icon, and preview image” collection and editable title/description.
decisions.note: The initial metadata behavior omitted most required metadata and description editing; corrected at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation offers editing “title/address/notes” but omits description and tags. Round 1 response asks for tags and editable title/description.
decisions.note: The initially presented edit fields were incomplete.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation: “delete with a confirmation step.”
decisions.note: Conforming delete behavior at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation merely lists “duplicate URLs” as handled. Round 1 response makes the behavior definite: re-saving must open the existing bookmark for editing and “never create another copy or silently replace information.”
decisions.note: The duplicate rule was underspecified; the client supplied the reference behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation only says “see all bookmarks.” Round 1 response expects each list item to show “title, description, tags, and site icon.”
decisions.note: The initial list presentation omitted required readability fields.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation says users can “open one in a new tab”; the response likewise expects selection to open the original page.
decisions.note: Opening the original URL is conforming; the new-tab detail is orthogonal.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation explicitly puts “tags” out of scope. Round 1 response requires bookmark tags, existing-tag suggestions, and tag filtering.
decisions.note: The client rejected an explicit exclusion of the tag feature set.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation limits search to “keyword across title/address.” Round 1 response adds description, notes, case-insensitivity, exact phrases, #tag, boolean operators, and grouping.
decisions.note: The initial search decision omitted required fields and query semantics.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation has no read-later behavior. Round 1 response requests “Read-later status, with a separate unread view and a way to mark items read.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing unread workflow at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation describes only per-bookmark operations. Round 1 response requires multi-selection and actions over “everything matching the current search or filter.”
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing selected-item and whole-filter bulk behaviors.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation fixes browsing to “newest first.” Round 1 response asks for “Sorting options, rather than always forcing newest-first.”
decisions.note: The client replaced a fixed ordering with selectable sorting.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation has generic notes only. Round 1 response requires notes that “contain formatting and display that formatting when viewed.”
decisions.note: Rendered markdown-style notes were missing from the initial scope.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation has no preservation facility. Round 1 response requests a local page copy, original-PDF handling, and Internet Archive preservation.
decisions.note: The client added both local and Internet Archive preservation.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation offers deletion but no archive. Round 1 response defines archive as reversible, hidden from normal browse/search, and available in its own view.
decisions.note: The complete archive lifecycle was absent initially.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation has no saved filters. Round 1 response requests saved combinations of searches and included/excluded tags.
decisions.note: Bundles/saved views were added by the client.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation makes browser/file import out of scope and does not offer export. Round 1 response requires standard browser bookmark import/export with import fidelity.
decisions.note: The client rejected the import exclusion and added the paired export requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation has no display preferences. Round 1 response asks for default sorting, item count, and text-size choices.
decisions.note: Personal display settings were missing from the initial specification.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation: “Save with automatic metadata” covering title, description, icon, preview, and editable title/description.
decisions.note: The revised save and metadata decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation: repeat save routes to the existing entry to edit—“never a copy, never a silent overwrite.”
decisions.note: The revised duplicate decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation includes tag assignment, live existing-tag suggestions, and tag filtering.
decisions.note: The revised tag workflow conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation specifies search across address/title/description/notes/tags, case-insensitivity, phrases, and #tag.
decisions.note: These revised search capabilities conform; boolean edge rules are classified separately.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation lists boolean search and grouping but does not state how ordinary words combine with #tag. Round 2 response requires implicit AND unless OR is explicit.
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing mixed-term combination rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation lists AND/OR/NOT but omits quoted-operator behavior. Round 2 response says quoted “AND”, “OR”, or “NOT” must be ordinary text.
decisions.note: The client corrected a separate boolean-token edge rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation includes mark read/unread and a dedicated unread view.
decisions.note: The revised read-later workflow conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation makes archive reversible, hides archived items from normal browse/search, provides a separate view and restore, and keeps delete distinct.
decisions.note: The archive/delete decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation says users can choose sorting.
decisions.note: Selectable sorting conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation lists bulk tagging but not tag removal. Round 2 response states bulk changes must support “removing tags as well as adding them.”
decisions.note: Bulk tag removal remained missing after the first revision.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation explicitly includes multi-select with “all matching.”
decisions.note: The revised specification correctly includes whole-filter bulk scope.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation supports saving search-and-tag combinations as named views.
decisions.note: Saved bundles/views conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation says formatted notes are rendered when viewed.
decisions.note: The revised rich-note behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation promises a “Local page copy” and original PDFs but does not define normal pages as a single file. Round 2 response requires a “self-contained HTML file.”
decisions.note: The client supplied the required preservation format.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation includes optional Internet Archive preservation.
decisions.note: Internet Archive support conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation includes standard browser bookmark import/export and preserves titles, tags, and original dates.
decisions.note: The revised import/export decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation includes default sort, items per view, and text size.
decisions.note: Display preferences conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation says each row shows title, description, tags, and site icon and opens the original page when activated.
decisions.note: The revised list presentation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation mentions editing collected title/description but not the bookmark address. Round 2 response requires editing “address as well as its title, description, tags, and note.”
decisions.note: The complete editable-field set remained absent after the first revision.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 presentation says FR-004 now covers editing address, title, description, tags, and note; round 3 client approves.
decisions.note: Corrected editable fields conform at final specification review.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 presentation adds both bulk add-tags and remove-tags; round 3 client approves.
decisions.note: Corrected bulk tag actions conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 presentation defines ordinary words plus #tag as implicit AND; round 3 client approves.
decisions.note: Corrected mixed-search semantics conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 presentation makes quoted AND/OR/NOT literal text; round 3 client approves.
decisions.note: Corrected quoted-operator behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 presentation specifies self-contained HTML for ordinary pages and original PDF storage for PDFs; round 3 client approves.
decisions.note: Corrected preservation format conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 plan uses a unique normalized URL and returns the existing bookmark on repeat save/edit; round 4 client says the plan supports the approved behavior.
decisions.note: Duplicate handling remains conforming at the plan gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 plan uses a tokenizer/parser and parameterized SQLite for implicit AND, quoted literals, precedence, #tag, phrases, and case-insensitivity; client approves.
decisions.note: Planned search behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 plan specifies original PDF streaming, self-contained HTML rendering, and best-effort Internet Archive submission; client approves the failure handling.
decisions.note: The preservation plan conforms as presented.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 plan says bulk actions accept an ID list or “all matching current query/filter” and support add/remove tags, read/unread, archive, and delete.
decisions.note: The planned bulk API conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 presentation calls US1+US2 the suggested MVP and says “A working product stops cleanly there.” Round 5 response says to implement all phases and that the MVP checkpoint “should be a validation point, not the stopping point for this cycle.”
decisions.note: At the task/implementation gate, the client rejected stopping after the save-and-duplicate subset and required delivery of the remaining approved reference features.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 presentation reports save, automatic metadata, editing/deletion, and duplicate re-save opening the existing bookmark; the client identifies no mismatch in this cluster.
decisions.note: Presented implementation of the save/edit/duplicate cluster conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 presentation reports cards, tag suggestions/filtering, and phrase/#tag/boolean/grouped search; the client identifies no mismatch in these behaviors.
decisions.note: Presented list, tag, and search implementation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 presentation reports All/Unread/Archive views and per-card read actions; no mismatch is raised for unread behavior.
decisions.note: Presented read-later implementation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 presentation reports a multi-select bulk bar with add/remove tags, read/unread, archive, and delete. The client’s objection is specifically to whole-filter selection beyond the current page.
decisions.note: Selected-bookmark bulk actions conform; whole-collection scope is classified separately.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 presentation claims multi-select/bulk support, but round 6 client observes that “Select all” selects only the visible page and requires actions over the entire current search/filter, including later pages.
decisions.note: Implementation review exposed that whole-filter bulk selection did not match the approved behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 presentation reports sorting, “Save current view,” and preferences for sort/page-size/text-size; the client raises no mismatch for them.
decisions.note: Presented sorting, bundles, and display settings conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 presentation calls local snapshots self-contained but admits cross-origin assets may retain original URLs. Round 6 client requires embedding them or marking the preservation incomplete/failed instead of successful.
decisions.note: The admitted external dependencies contradicted successful single-file preservation.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 presentation reports a non-blocking “Send to archive.org” action with surfaced failure status.
decisions.note: Presented Internet Archive behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 presentation reports separate Archive behavior and Import/Export; verification says archived items are excluded from normal browse/search and import fidelity is tested.
decisions.note: Presented archive and browser-file transfer behaviors conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 presentation says “Select all N matching” now sends a filter selector and acts on every matching bookmark beyond the page; round 7 client says both corrections match approved behavior.
decisions.note: The implementation correction for whole-filter bulk actions conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 presentation says resources are embedded and verified, with any remaining external image/style/font causing failed status and no successful file; round 7 client accepts the correction.
decisions.note: The corrected preservation success criteria conform.
